summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, prior pancreas and failed kidney transplants, coronary artery disease, and systolic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction was admitted for lethargy and hypotension. She presented with shock, acute respiratory failure, and signs of acute on chronic heart failure with bilateral pleural effusions and pulmonary edema. She was started on vasopressor support with levophed, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and a right femoral central line was placed. Blood cultures initially flagged coagulase-negative staph but later cultures and dialysis fluid were negative, suggesting contamination. Peritoneal dialysis was resumed, and she gradually improved. Vasopressors were weaned, mental status normalized, and warfarin was restarted at 1 mg. She was discharged to extended care with plans for follow-up in transplant, nephrology, and cardiology clinics.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
